title: lara croft and the guardian of light
text: Great twin stick shooter with lots of collectibles.  You can power up your character with health upgrades, ammo upgrades and even find and use more weapons.  It has online multiplayer CO-OP which is awesome.  Playing coop you WILL have to use team work.  You either play as Lara Croft or Totec.  Lara mainly uses guns and grappling hooks while Totec uses spears and shields. In coop Lara will use her grappling hook and Totec must walk on it like a tight rope to advance in puzzles or platforming.  Totec uses his shield to help boost Lara upward and throw his spears on the walls for Lara to do some parkour action.  Both of these mechanics are a must and can not be avoided. Online or local coop in this is absolutely fantastic and a must play for people looking for some coop fun.  Lots of stuff to do with a story and there are fun bosses to battle as well.  Can grab the complete pack for $20, but goes on sale a lot for $5.  Extremely recommended!  Play this game.

title: lara croft and the guardian of light
text: My all-time favourite twin-stick shooter! Fantastic gameplay in both single player and co-op modes. Maps are slightly differnet in co=op, requiring the abilities of both characters to progress. A couple of levels are a bit wonky in co-op because the game tries to keep both players on the screen and in some areas ends up pulling one to his/her death. There are a good variety of weapons and special items which grant bonuses, like increased speed or health/ammo regeneration, but I found myself sticking to a couple of favourite weapons and I got a really good special item early on, which regenerated health and ammo, and used that throughout most of the game. Lara's twin handguns and Toltec's spear have infinite ammo. Only the other weapons require ammo pickups. Weapon unlocks are specific to the character so levels have to be replayed in order for both characters to get them. Puzzles and platforming are simple enough, as the main focus is on the action, but they are a bit more challenging in co-op. Challenges for extra unlocks and 100% completion were not overly difficult, and thus were mostly enjoyable. I've only played local co-op so I cannot comment on the online functionality, but I'm guessing there isn't much online activity due to the age of the game. I doubt I would have played with random people anyway,. Local co-op with friends or family is the way to go, imo. My play time doesn't accurately reflect the time I put into this game. I've played though to 100% completion in both single and co-op modes several times on another computer. Despite a couple of minor faults, this game is a 10/10 for me!

title: lara croft and the guardian of light
text: This is my favorite "surprise" of 2010.  I'd never played a Lara Croft game, but as soon I played the demo for this I wanted to keep playing.  Throw in co-op and I was sold. GAMEPLAY:  It has the isometric view of Diablo, with the twin-stick movement/shooting of Geometry Wars, and platforming and puzzles and treasure hunting and customizable weapon load-outs. The hardest puzzles are in optional challenge rooms, so even if you're not great at solving puzzles, you can keep playing. CO-OP: Each player has unique abilties, but they have to use their abilities in concert to get through the game and solve puzzles.  For example, Lara has a grappling hook, which she can use to create rope bridges for her partner, Totec, to cross. Meanwhile, Totec has spears that he can throw into walls which Lara can use as platforms to reach higher places. There's also separate scoreboards, so you can even compete against each other for the highest score while solving puzzles together! Play it!

title: left 4 dead 2
text: Although I don't have a lot of hours on this game, I think this is probably one of the best Co Op zombie survival games. The run and gun aspect is really fun, and some of the guns and melee weapons are really cool to mess around with. The workshop for this game is really good, ranging from hentai noises for witch to a different, more epic ending to The Sacrifice. It also includes like 18 mutations, and it comes with the Left 4 Dead 1 campaign, too. I mean, come on. You're basically getting two incredibly great games for 20 dollars (Or 1.99 if you buy it on sale, like I did). The campaign on its own is great, for both games, mind you, but it also has other game modes. Survival, Versus, and Scavenge (I'm pretty sure those are the only other ones, but there are realism variations plus Mutation). It might sound like a small amount, but you'll be playing Versus trying to master the Special Infected, or Survival trying to get the best time to flaunt off to friends and players you meet online. There are a lot of achievements that seem like a waste of time to get, but to me I like getting achievements. A lot of the hours at the time of posting this are basically only from trying to get achievements, survival, and versus. The comedic aspect is really nice as well, with Ellis' random stories in the middle of the apocalypse, to the song available on Jukeboxes Re: Your Brains. If you ever find a way to master EVERY valve made survival map (Which is highly unlikelay, but probably very possible), then go back to what I said about the workshop, check the workshop, and voila, new maps to get annoyed at. The graphics, while not as great as a 2017 game (obviously) are actually very good for a 2009 game. The co op is so great, whether it be from strangers or with friends you already know. You can always find something to do in Left 4 Dead, and chances are you might never be bored. Seeing as a lot of my friends have hundreds or even a thousand hours on this game, I think that probably proves the point I'm trying to make. Another masterpiece by Valve. Thank you for bestowing this beautiful game upon us. TL;DR - Definitely buy this game, great co op, great gamemodes, 10/10.

text: This game relates in the concepts of: -Jet Set Radio: Music and Art style, Character Design -Super Smash Bros.: Original 4 Player Fighting Game, Anauncer, Character Select Screen, Replayability. -DiveKick: One hit kill. So use caution... -PONG: Ball Physics, At first this game seems pretty simple, dodge the ball and hit it to the oponent, and that is pretty much it really... Newcomers to the game will get hit by some slow moving balls, trying to see the ball coming towards them. The fact is, that the ball will reach incredible speeds, making it litterally impossible to see coming. However it is not impossible to predict. The fighting term "yomi" is a perfect word to describe this game, "yomi" meaning predicting your opponent's actions. Although this game doesn't make it totaly impossible, there is a bar at the bottom of the screen that will fill up during a hit, sometimes quick, sometimes slow. Once it fills the ball will fly out. many players abuse this to hit the ball in the same place, I assume programmers saw this so they created a shield you can activate for a brief period at the cost of your meter, from 1/4 to full. If the other player hit's this, he will be stunned and sent towards the projectile, most of the time... This game has tons of replayability, I really recomend it.

title: limbo
text: It's a little overpriced for the short and sweet experience, but it's also very good. Minimalism at its finest: not a single word of dialogue (so no translation issues once you hit 'new game'), few sound effects, and one action button. It is subtle, but surprisingly disturbing in some parts (that spider in the previews made my skin crawl). What little we learn about the setting is shown, not told. The difficulty curve spikes at the end, but in a good way-- even the puzzles that seemed impossible always had a solution within the simple physics engine. I recommend it if you have the spare cash and a spare evening.
